title: Local trivialization determines maximal localization and residue rank
statement: Let $E$ be a commutative ring, $P$ an $E$-module, $\mathfrak q$ a maximal ideal, $f\in E\setminus\mathfrak q$, and $r\geq0$ an integer. Suppose $P_f\cong E_f^{\oplus r}$, where localization away from $f$ is [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away]. Write $S=E\setminus\mathfrak q$, $E_{\mathfrak q}=S^{-1}E$, $P_{\mathfrak q}=S^{-1}P$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization], [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], and $k_{\mathfrak q}=E/\mathfrak q$. Then $P_{\mathfrak q}\cong E_{\mathfrak q}^{\oplus r}$. The canonical map $P/\mathfrak qP\longrightarrow P_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak qP_{\mathfrak q}$, $[p]\longmapsto[p/1]$, is an isomorphism over $k_{\mathfrak q}\cong E_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak qE_{\mathfrak q}$, and $P/\mathfrak qP$ has dimension $r$ over $k_{\mathfrak q}$ [def-weil-vector-space-dimension].

source.place: Tag 02M9 (algebra-lemma-locally-free-semi-local-free), proof, first hint: maximal residue modules have the constant rank; localization comparisons made explicit.

proof.text: Put $k=E/\mathfrak q$. By [lem-weil-common-extension-fields-quotient-field], $k$ is a field. Thus every $s\in S=E\setminus\mathfrak q$ has nonzero, invertible image $\bar s\in k$; in particular $S$ is multiplicatively closed and contains every $f^n$. Using the fraction relations in [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away] and [def-weil-pbc-module-localization], the formula $j:E_f\to E_{\mathfrak q}$, $a/f^n\mapsto a/f^n$, defines a ring map: any annihilating power of $f$ becomes a unit, so equal fractions have equal images. The fraction formula $\lambda:E_{\mathfrak q}\to k$, $a/s\mapsto\bar a\bar s^{-1}$, is also a well-defined ring map: an equality witnessed by $u\in S$ remains an equality after division by $\bar u\bar s\bar t$ in $k$. It is surjective since $a/1\mapsto\bar a$. Its kernel is $\mathfrak qE_{\mathfrak q}$: it kills every generator from $\mathfrak q$, and $\lambda(a/s)=0$ implies $a\in\mathfrak q$, hence $a/s=(a/1)(1/s)\in\mathfrak qE_{\mathfrak q}$. Consequently it induces the asserted canonical ring identification $E_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak qE_{\mathfrak q}\cong k$, inverse to $\bar a\mapsto[a/1]$.

source.place: Tag 02M9 (lemma-locally-free-semi-local-free), first proof hint; explicit residue-ring calculation using the fraction construction of Definition 07JZ (definition-localization-module).

proof.text:
Regard $E_{\mathfrak q}$ as an $E_f$-algebra via $j$. Write $C=E_{\mathfrak q}\otimes_{E_f}P_f$ using [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. The formulas
$$L:C\longrightarrow P_{\mathfrak q},\quad (a/s)\otimes(p/f^n)\longmapsto ap/(sf^n),\qquad B:P_{\mathfrak q}\longrightarrow C,\quad p/s\longmapsto(1/s)\otimes(p/1)$$
define inverse $E_{\mathfrak q}$-linear maps. Here are the well-definedness checks from [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] and [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away]. For $L$, a relation $f^h(f^{n'}p-f^np')=0$ becomes zero in $P_{\mathfrak q}$ because $f^h$ is invertible there; a relation between $a/s$ and $a'/s'$ is treated by the same cancellation of its witness $u\in S$. Additivity follows from the fraction addition formulas, and balancing by $b/f^h\in E_f$ gives $abp/(sf^{n+h})$ on either side. For $B$, if $p/s=p'/s'$ with witness $u\in S$, the difference of the proposed images is
$$(1/(uss'))\otimes\bigl(u(s'p-sp')/1\bigr)=0.$$
The fraction addition and scalar formulas give linearity. Finally $LB(p/s)=p/s$, and on a generating pure tensor
$$BL((a/s)\otimes(p/f^n))=(a/(sf^n))\otimes(p/1)=(a/s)\otimes(p/f^n),$$
the last equality being the tensor balancing relation for the unit $f^n\in E_f$. Thus $L$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 00DK (lemma-tensor-localization), explicit inverse calculation; adapted to the scalar tower E to E_f to E_q, with Definition 07JZ (definition-localization-module).

proof.text: Choose the $r$ basis vectors $b_1,\ldots,b_r$ of $P_f$ supplied by the assumed isomorphism $P_f\cong E_f^{\oplus r}$; basis means unique finite coordinates as in [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-free-module-base-change-free] with $R=E_f$, $A=E_{\mathfrak q}$, $F=P_f$ and index set $\{1,\ldots,r\}$. Its statement gives the basis $(1\otimes b_i)_i$ of $C$. Through $L$ these give a basis $v_i=L(1\otimes b_i)$ of $P_{\mathfrak q}$, and hence an $E_{\mathfrak q}$-linear isomorphism $P_{\mathfrak q}\cong E_{\mathfrak q}^{\oplus r}$.

source.place: Tag 02M9 (lemma-locally-free-semi-local-free), first proof hint, base change of the chosen principal-local basis; Mathlib Module.Basis.baseChange supplies precisely this operation.

proof.text:
Here $\mathfrak qP$ and $\mathfrak qP_{\mathfrak q}$ mean submodules of finite sums of products $ap$, with $a\in\mathfrak q$ and $p$ in the respective module. The map $p\mapsto[p/1]$ kills $\mathfrak qP$ and induces $\eta:P/\mathfrak qP\to P_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak qP_{\mathfrak q}$. Define
$$d:P_{\mathfrak q}\longrightarrow P/\mathfrak qP,\qquad d(p/s)=\bar s^{-1}[p].$$
It is well defined: if $u(s'p-sp')=0$, reduction modulo $\mathfrak qP$ followed by multiplication by $(\bar u\bar s\bar s')^{-1}$ gives $\bar s^{-1}[p]=\bar s'^{-1}[p']$. The addition formula for fractions proves additivity, and $d((a/t)(p/s))=(\bar a/\bar t)d(p/s)$ proves scalar compatibility through $\lambda$. In particular $d$ kills every $a(p/s)$ with $a\in\mathfrak q$, and so induces $\bar d$ on the target quotient. Now $\bar d\eta([p])=[p]$. Conversely, for $s\in S$, choose $t\in E$ lifting $\bar s^{-1}$; then $ts-1\in\mathfrak q$ and
$$[tp/1]-[p/s]=[(ts-1)p/s]=0.$$
Hence $\eta\bar d([p/s])=[p/s]$. These calculations prove both that the specified canonical map is bijective and that it is $k$-linear under the ring identification in step 1. No finiteness assumption on $P$ has been used here.

source.place: Tag 02M9 (lemma-locally-free-semi-local-free), first proof hint: explicit comparison of maximal residue modules, using the fractions of Definition 07JZ (definition-localization-module).

proof.text:
The coordinate isomorphism from step 3 carries $\mathfrak qP_{\mathfrak q}$ onto $(\mathfrak qE_{\mathfrak q})^{\oplus r}$. Indeed a finite sum of $\mathfrak q$-multiples has each coordinate in $\mathfrak qE_{\mathfrak q}$; conversely expand each of the finitely many coordinates as a finite sum of $\mathfrak q$-multiples and put those terms in the corresponding coordinate vector. Reducing coordinates therefore gives
$$P_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak qP_{\mathfrak q}\cong(E_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak qE_{\mathfrak q})^{\oplus r}\cong k^{\oplus r}.$$
For completeness, the coordinate quotient map is onto by lifting each coordinate, and its kernel is exactly the coordinate ideal submodule just computed. Composing with $\eta$ gives $P/\mathfrak qP\cong k^{\oplus r}$. The inverse images of the $r$ standard coordinate vectors form a basis by unique coordinates [def-weil-pbc-free-module]; hence [def-weil-vector-space-dimension] gives dimension $r$. When $r=0$, all these direct sums and coordinate families are empty and the same computations give the zero modules. The zero ring has no maximal ideal, so it supplies no exceptional case.
